name: bypass: pnpm --dir publish
note: Historical bypass: the legacy regex never saw a publish behind a value-taking global option.

name: bypass: npm --prefix publish
note: Same class as --dir: the option value sat where the old code read a verb.

name: bypass: yarn publish
note: yarn is a package manager too; the old matcher only knew pnpm/npm.

name: bypass: bash -c publish
note: The wrapper is unwrapped into its script, so the inner publish is judged as itself.

name: bypass: bash -c merge
note: Merges journal rather than ask; the wrapper must not hide the verdict.

name: bypass: quoted cd push
note: A quoted cd target cannot be resolved and HEAD is implicit, so fail closed.

name: carried: publish behind a --filter VALUE
note: Carried from the B3/B4 reviews: `run` is the VALUE of --filter, not a script runner, so this is a real publish. Today it reads as allow because the runner scan consumed the option value; task B5 makes the runner read positional (the resolved subcommand slot) so the value cannot suppress the verb.

name: carried: interpreter inline program pushing a protected branch

args.command: python3 -c "import os; os.system('git push origin master')"

note: DELIBERATE residual pinned by task B5 (the code comment in rules.ts names this class). `python3 -c` is an interpreter inline program: the guard cannot read the language, and an inline program is lexically indistinguishable from the `node -e` MENTION case that must stay quiet. Gating it would require interpreting the program text.

name: carried: node -e inline program tagging a release
note: Same deliberate residual as the python3 row: the quoted program is data, and the deleted `multiline-quoted` suite pinned `node -e` as not-gated. `python3 deploy.py` is equally opaque, so gating one inline form would not close the class.

name: carried: quoted gh api branch-protection delete
note: The quoted path is the point: the shape gate reads the quote-stripped surface, but the protected-branch LOCATOR must read the raw segment text, or `gh api -X DELETE "<path>"` collapses to `gh api -X DELETE` and the deletion is allowed.

name: carried: quoted data mentioning a release

args.command: gh pr create --body "ported the gh release create flow onto the parsed rule engine"

note: Quoted text is DATA: a PR body that describes `gh release create` must not fire the release rule. Pinned so a future raw-text matcher cannot regress it.

name: carried: git -C with an unexpanded dir and a feature refspec
note: Decision recorded, not silently accepted: the refspec (feature/x) is itself provable and unprotected, so the ask is an over-block caused by the segment-level ambiguity of the unexpanded -C value. It stays fail-closed because narrowing it would have to exempt an ambiguity class that also covers an expandable refspec (`git push origin $BRANCH`), which must keep asking. Task B5 touches rules.ts only for the publish-runner positional fix, so the narrowing is left as a named follow-up.

name: over-block: dry run
note: A dry run changes nothing but is still recorded.

name: over-block: leak-scan grep
note: A mention-only verb scanning for secret-shaped strings is not an access.

name: over-block: prose write

args.content: we rotated the auth material today

note: Non-shell tools are judged on the path field, never on content; the OS temp dir is exempt from containment.

name: false positive to keep fixed: feature push from a protected repo
note: The 58-event false positive: an explicit non-protected refspec is the target, whatever branch the repo is checked out on.
